Both included in "Generate Diagnostic Bundle .zip" as `soar_events.txt` + `firewall_rules.txt`.
- **Memory Injection Scanner enrichment (`modules/mem_inject_scanner.py`, MINJ)** — `_enrich_process(pid)` collects: exe path, cmdline (first 8 tokens), username, status, thread count, process age (h/m/s), parent name+PID, child count, loaded DLL count, active TCP connections (up to 8), RSS KB + VMS MB. `_predict_technique(proc_name, size, protect, ctx)` classifies likely technique (high-value system process / C2 carrier / process hollowing / packed binary / reflective DLL / shellcode stub) and builds MITRE sub-technique list (T1055 base + T1055.001, T1055.012, T1071, T1078.003 conditionally). Alert messages are now multi-line with all enriched fields; `predicted_technique` key in `details`.

## LATEST (v1.3.0 — Eco stampede fix, Live-Fire Sandbox, online-AI consult, resource strip)
- **Eco Mode auto-on + sequential wake-up** — `Config.eco_mode` (default True, Settings ▸ Performance toggle) starts the app with heavy scanners paused for a fast, responsive launch; `app._load_modules` fires `MainWindow.startup_eco_requested` (queued signal) after `start_enabled()`. Turning Eco OFF now uses **`core/eco_wakeup.py:EcoWakeupWorker`** (QThread): wakes paused modules ONE AT A TIME with a per-module health-gate (`health>0`+running, else `status=="error"`/2.5 s timeout), signals `module_waking`/`module_ready`/`wakeup_complete`. Fixes the "memory stampede" that froze the UI when ~19 threads rescanned at once.
- **Live-Fire Sandbox & Editor (`gui/sandbox_editor.py`, SBOX)** — standalone PySide6 module isolation + hot-swap editor. On launch: `manager.stop_all()`, mutes the EventBus (swaps `bus.publish` for a no-op, restored on close), and overrides the brand banner to "⚠️ DIAGNOSTIC OVERRIDE: TESTING IN PROGRESS". Left module tree · center `QPlainTextEdit` with a `PythonHighlighter` · right test/history console. Buttons: Open · Run Isolated Test (`self_test()` on a decoupled thread, stdout/stderr captured) · Apply Changes (QMessageBox warning → **`ast.parse()` gate** → write → history → `importlib.reload()` + rebind + restart) · Revert to Previous (in-mem + temp backups) · View History. Reload/restart failures are pushed onto the live alert feed. Launch from the FORENSICS menu ("Live-Fire Sandbox & Editor…"), a module window's "✎ Edit code (Sandbox)" button, or `python -m angerona.gui.sandbox_editor`.
- **Online AI consult (`engines/ai_consult.py` + `gui/ai_consult_dialog.py`)** — user-initiated (= consented) online consult, **Anthropic/Claude first**, then OpenAI → OpenRouter → Gemini → local Ollama fallback (stdlib urllib; keys from Settings ▸ API Keys in the DPAPI store). `AIConsultDialog` runs it off-thread and offers **Save to computer / Discard**. Surfaced as: Threat-Intel dashboard "🌐 Consult AI"; CVE Deep-Analysis window "🌐 Consult AI" (fallback-OK) + "💡 AI Proposed Solution" (online-only) that build a full CVE fix/patch file; and alert-detail "🔎 Research".
- **Alert action buttons everywhere (`gui/pages.py`)** — `AlertDetailDialog` now carries **Allow · Block · Analyze · Research** (Block/Analyze work standalone via the bus/`AnalysisWorker`, or reuse the AlertsPanel when opened from it). A module window's recent-events feed is now clickable and opens the SAME detail dialog, so module alerts get the same actions as the main Live Alerts feed.
- **Bottom bars upgraded (`gui/pages.py`)** — StatusStrip chips are clickable (`_ClickableChip`) → open that module's full window (`ModuleInspector`: details, live alerts, self-test, restart, Edit-code). New **`ResourceStrip`** second row shows per-module resource-intensity 0–100% (0=stopped→red, low→green, busy→amber→orange-red; heuristic = heaviness weight + live event rate). `ModulesPanel` gains a **Sort by: Name / On-Off / Status / Category** selector.
- **Console commands (`core/commands.py`)** — `intel`/`kev`/`fetchintel` (summarise host-applicable CISA KEV from `shared_logs/upstream_threats.json`), `consult <q>` (online AI, Claude-first), `resources`/`resmon`/`load` (per-module intensity snapshot).
- **Deception hygiene** — canaries + honeytokens are now written **HIDDEN|SYSTEM** (`deception.py`, `smart_deception.py`) so they never clutter Desktop/Documents. **Red-team auto-cleanup** (`shark/red_team.py`): every marker is `_redteam_*` + hidden, swept on start (orphans from crashed runs), on `stop_and_clean()`, and ~55 s after a drill ends (post-detection settle) — the drill no longer litters Documents.
- **Tooling** — `tools/compile_check.py` + `run-compile-check.bat`: fast stdlib syntax gate over `src/angerona` (run before `run-selfcheck.bat`).
- **Fix — Settings button (defensive):** `_open_settings` is now wrapped so a construction error surfaces in a dialog + console instead of silently doing nothing (the classic "button does nothing"). (Prior root cause — `apply_theme` signature — remains fixed.)
- **Situational awareness — Threat Posture score (`core/posture.py`)** — composite 0–100 indicator under the brand (band + colour: Secure/Guarded/Elevated/High/Critical), updated each tick from active HIGH/CRITICAL detections + degraded/stopped modules + host-applicable KEV count + ATT&CK heat. Click it for a factor breakdown. Never raises (missing signal = 0 contribution).
- **Situational awareness — CRITICAL tray notifications (`main_window._notify_critical`)** — new CRITICAL bus detections raise a Windows tray/toast (`QSystemTrayIcon.showMessage`, 8 s throttle) so the operator stays aware while minimized.
- **Situational awareness — Top Talkers (`gui/top_talkers.py`)** — live "who is my machine talking to": established outbound connections grouped by process, untrusted-external count flagged red, interface type, optional reverse-DNS, 4 s refresh. Opens from the FORENSICS menu ("Top Talkers — outbound network…"). psutil walk + `net_interfaces` enrichment.
- **Research follow-up chat (`gui/ai_consult_dialog.py`)** — the AI consult/Research window gains a "💬 Ask AI" button that reveals a prompt bar for a multi-turn conversation (context carried across turns) alongside Save/Discard.
- **Fix — splitter drag** — the Modules|Alerts and body|Console `QSplitter`s now use non-opaque resize + `setChildrenCollapsible(False)` + a 7 px handle + per-panel minimum sizes, fixing the glitchy/unreliable panel-resize drag (heavy tables were thrashing under opaque resize).
- **Adaptive Resource Governor (`modules/resource_governor.py`, GOV)** — samples this process's CPU every 5 s and, under sustained load (>22%/core), raises `BaseModule._throttle` on heavy **non-critical** running modules so their `self.sleep()` loops run up to 6× slower (lower CPU); relaxes back to 1× when load drops (<10%/core). Works in BOTH Eco and normal mode. NEVER throttles the real-time protection path (SOAR, Watchdog, Heartbeat, IPC Guard, AI Triage, Active Deception, Ransomware Heuristics, AMSI, Fast-Path, Shadow Shield). Cooperative only — never suspends/kills threads; fail-open.
- **`BaseModule` throttle hook** — new `self._throttle` (default 1.0) + `set_throttle()`; `sleep()` multiplies its wait by it, so any module using `self.sleep()` for cadence is governable for free.
- **Baseline perf** — Shadow Shield's Documents/Desktop stat-walk moved 5 s → 15 s (~3× less steady CPU; VSS + RANS remain the real ransomware net); Smart Deception decoy-check 1 s → 2.5 s. Posture score caches its KEV file read (mtime + 30 s TTL) and, with the ResourceStrip, now refreshes every ~4 s instead of every tick — removing a per-second disk read/compute the first v1.3.0 cut introduced.
- **Black Box auto-launch** — source runs `blackbox_recorder.py`; frozen releases run the separately packaged `AngeronaBlackBox.exe` rather than relaunching the main executable. The sidecar starts ~800 ms after first paint, is single-instance guarded and fail-open, and captures startup output under `<data_dir>/logs/blackbox.log`. Gated by `Config.blackbox_enabled` (default True; Settings ▸ Performance ▸ Black Box toggle).
- **Black Box resilience + reach** — QtCharts is optional. The recorder reads the canonical protected runtime boundary only and writes its exports, archive, ring buffer, startup log, and diagnostics there; frozen code never writes beside the executable.
- **Crash/stall evidence → Black Box** — `core/crashlog.py` (already installed in `__main__`) mirrors unhandled exceptions / faulthandler native faults / Qt-fatal to `<data_dir>/logs/crash.log` + `diagnostics/crash.log`; `uiwatchdog` writes `diagnostics/not_responding.log` on a GUI stall. NEW: `MainWindow._blackbox_feed()` appends every CRITICAL notification (and non-fatal UI-refresh errors) to `diagnostics/runtime_alerts.log`, which the Black Box tails — so "went non-responsive / got a CRITICAL" always reaches the recorder.
- **Anti-crash under load** — `MainWindow._refresh` is fully wrapped (per-panel guarded) so a panel raising under a data flood can't propagate out of the QTimer and kill the app; worst case one repaint tick is skipped. EventBus already rings at 500 with INFO backpressure.
- **Governor is now memory-aware + more aggressive** — thresholds CPU>18%/core or RAM≥85% throttle a step; severe (CPU>36%/core or RAM≥92%) jumps 2 steps; max slowdown 8× (was 6×); sample 4 s. This sheds load before the machine thrashes/OOMs (the actual cause of the random crashes).
- **Desktop launcher safety** — the legacy-named `create-blackbox-launcher.ps1` now creates only the supported Angerona launcher. The elevated suite owns the Black Box child; no separate unelevated shortcut is created against administrator-only runtime evidence.

## LATEST (v1.3.0 cont. — mobile remote control, Linux eBPF, SGX confidential compute)
- **Mobile Response Bridge (`modules/mobile_bridge.py`, MOB_BRDG)** — E2EE remote orchestration over Signal (`signal-cli`). Opt-in (`Config.mobile_enabled`, Settings ▸ Mobile Integration; fields locked until enabled; 4-digit **PIN is DPAPI-wrapped** in the protected credential store). Thread always runs but self-gates (idles when disabled/unconfigured). HIGH/CRITICAL bus alerts → `neutralize_telemetry()` → random single-use 4-digit token in `self.pending_alerts`; TTL sweep every 10 s prunes tokens >10 min and auto-SUSPENDs + notifies; >3 alerts/60 s aggregate into one digest text. Command parser (from the operator number only; unknown/failed input silently discarded + logged as "Spoof/Unauthorized Access Attempt" with msg SHA): **HELP** (verbatim menu, bypasses tokens), **STATUS** (posture+KEV), **DIAG** (proc CPU/RAM/threads), **ECO ON/OFF** (drives the Governor throttle), **LOCKDOWN <PIN>** (host isolation directive), **KILL/SUSPEND <TOKEN> <PIN>** (signed mitigation directive on the bus, token erased), **ROLLBACK <TOKEN> <PIN>** (Shadow Shield `trigger_rollback`), **MUTE <TOKEN>** (15-min per-module suppression). signal-cli runs as short subprocesses off the UI thread.
- **Linux eBPF sensor (`modules/ebpf_sensor.py`, EBPF)** — headless-Linux node sensor using BCC: inline eBPF C hooks `execve` (PID/UID/argv0) + `tcp_sendmsg` (PID/dst/port) with `BPF_PERF_OUTPUT`, kernel-side noise drop; `perf_buffer_poll` → Angerona `Event`s emitted on the bus (RBRG forwards to the Windows GUI). Opt-in (`Config.ebpf_enabled`, Settings ▸ System). Frees BPF maps on stop; wraps BCC init in try/except → health 10 % + graceful idle without root / headers / BCC; healthy-inert on Windows.
- **Confidential Compute — Intel SGX / Gramine (`core/sgx_guard.py` + `angerona.manifest.template`)** — `is_confidential_compute_active()` (checks `/dev/attestation/*` + Gramine env) for app.py / the posture dashboard; `SgxEnclaveGuard` generates an AES-256 key strictly in enclave memory and best-effort patches the MEMC `:memory:` SQLite to SQLCipher (`PRAGMA key`), no-op outside an enclave. The manifest graminizes the Python runtime (2 G enclave, 128 threads), maps `/src` read-only + an encrypted tmpfs, seals the IPC key to MRENCLAVE, allows the live `flight-recorder.db`, and keeps loopback (`:47921`) intact.

## LATEST (v1.2.0 — behavioural tuning, VPN awareness, hardware integrity, multi-node)
- **TUNE (`modules/behavioral_tuner.py`)** — Learning Engine + Safe-Path Interceptor (inverse of FPTH). Silent-audit window (default 7d) builds a 3-way `behavioral_baseline` (SQLite): SHA-256 hash + parent→child lineage + network /24-subnet+port. `check_event()`/`is_known_good()` downgrade a perfect match to INFO so backpressure drops it *before* Ollama; drift handler refreshes a hash silently on benign auto-update. `export_wfp_rules()` / `export_kernel_rules()` emit Ring-0 offload payloads (WFPC / AngeronaSensor.sys). Module-global `get_tuner()` lets `ai_triage` skip inference on baselined events (fail-open).
- **HEAL (`modules/self_healer.py`)** — Self-Debugging Co-Pilot (Try→Heal→Stage). Tails `diagnostics/crash_snapshots/`, packs traceback+source into a constrained Ollama prompt, `ast`-validates the returned code, and STAGES it to `staged_patches/<MOD>_fix_v<N>.py` (never overwrites live) + HIGH alert. GUI "Apply Patch" is the human gate.
- **SHDW (`modules/shadow_shield.py`)** — ransomware file shielding: delta version cache (`trigger_rollback()` restores pre-encryption copies) + quiet VSS snapshots (WMI/`vssadmin`). NEVER deletes shadow copies.
- **SDEC (`modules/smart_deception.py`)** — hyper-contextual honeytokens: samples Documents *names* only → local Ollama invents blended decoy names → drops into Desktop/Documents/%APPDATA%; any touch ⇒ CRITICAL. Static fallback list if Ollama down.
- **CHAOS (`modules/chaos_harness.py`)** — security chaos engineering "bug killer": on a slow cycle fires SAFE probes (APID cooperative drill signal — never a real hook; high-entropy DNS → NDRD; EICAR write → FIM/AMSI) and verifies the detector echoes on the bus within a timeout; missing echo ⇒ blind-sensor alert.
- **RBRG (`modules/remote_bridge.py`)** — secure multi-node telemetry forwarding. SENDER polls the bus and forwards HIGH/CRITICAL to the main PC; RECEIVER binds a LAN port, authenticates via shared-key HMAC challenge/response (extends AUTH), and republishes with `node_origin`/`hostname`. OFF by default (`enabled_by_default=False`); refuses to open the network without `ANGERONA_BRIDGE_MODE` + peer/port + `ANGERONA_BRIDGE_KEY`/`bridge.key`. Drops+logs unauthenticated peers.
- **HWID (`modules/hardware_crypto.py`)** — hardware-rooted integrity. DPAPI-wraps the AUTH IPC key to a user/host-bound sidecar `ipc_auth.key.dpapi` (win32crypt → ctypes fallback; verifies round-trip; live key untouched). `bind_db_key_to_tpm()` outlines TPM 2.0 sealing of the DB key via tpm2-pytss. Inert (no crash) off-Windows.
- **Headless mode (`core/headless.py`, `__main__.py --headless`)** — builds Config/EventBus/FlightRecorder/incidents/attack_tracker/remediation_log/ModuleManager WITHOUT importing PySide6; starts enabled modules; blocks until SIGINT/SIGTERM. For silent sensor / home-server nodes (pair with RBRG SENDER).
- **VPN awareness (`core/net_interfaces.py`)** — psutil-only interface classifier (Physical/Virtual_VPN/Loopback via name/OUI/point-to-point heuristics, 30 s cache). `network_monitor` stamps `interface_type` on NET events; `ai_triage` passes it into the Ollama prompt; **FPTH rule #18 (split-tunnel abuse)** — `detect_split_tunnel(pid)` fires CRITICAL when one PID holds concurrent VPN + physical-external connections.
- **GUI (`gui/pages.py`, `core/analysis_worker.py`)** — Alerts panel gains a 7th **Analyze** column: `AnalysisWorker` (QThread) runs dual-stage deep triage (local llama3:8b → cloud CTI if confidence <70 or UNKNOWN) off the GUI thread; button disables to "Analyzing…" so the GPU queue can't be spammed. `MarqueeLabel` slowly scrolls long alert text in the detail dialog. Remote alerts show a `⇠node_origin` tag.
- **Fix — Settings button:** `MainWindow.apply_theme()` now takes an optional `theme` arg; `SettingsDialog._save` passed one, so any theme-change Save previously raised `TypeError` and the dialog never closed/applied. Settings now work.

## CYCLE 8 — LOCAL FLEET PREVIEW, RESPONSE SAFETY, AND OPERATOR GUIDANCE

- Settings has one canonical owner per capability. Overview and Information
  tabs provide search, definitions, procedures, verification, privacy boundaries,
  and Take me there navigation. Advanced Console is diagnostic-only where
  Settings owns configuration.
- Explicit X/Close/Cancel actions must call `close()` so PanelRevealOverlay can
  perform the reverse animation. Do not bypass QEvent.Close with accept/reject
  for animated dialogs.
- Every QApplication entry point must install `install_global_window_reveal`;
  visible standalone launches use `show_with_window_reveal`. Reused dialogs and
  overlapping/nested windows are handled by the shared coordinator. Do not
  install a second coordinator inside an embedded window when MainWindow
  already owns the application-wide event filter.
- `core/fleet_control_plane.py` and `core/fleet_service.py` implement an opt-in,
  loopback-only fleet preview. Requests cover the complete path and query,
  payload digest, timestamp, and nonce. Replay, staleness, tampering,
  cross-tenant access, identity-key conflict, quarantine, and revocation fail
  closed. This is not production mTLS or an internet-facing service.
- `core/response_broker.py` is the typed enterprise response boundary. Never
  add a generic command/shell operation. Live operations need independent
  approval; high/critical operations require two distinct non-requester
  approvers. Preview validates but never invokes a handler.
- `core/identity_analytics.py` tokenizes accounts and sources before retention
  and detects password spray, distributed account attacks, repeated failures,
  new privileged sources, and interactive service-account use. Never accept
  passwords, tokens, or credential material as analytics input.
- `core/network_behavior.py` tokenizes process/destination identity before
  retention and detects periodic beacons, private lateral fanout, external
  fanout, and asymmetric upload. Never store packet payloads in this layer.
- `core/exposure_management.py` owns durable vulnerability lifecycle state:
  owner, deadline, optimistic version, bounded exception expiry, closure digest,
  and authenticated audit receipt. Never mark resolved without SHA-256 evidence.
- `core/plugin_lifecycle.py` stages the exact verified source and parsed signed
  manifest, revalidates before activation, never imports code, and quarantines
  revocation/tampering. Preserve signed entrypoint names; reject collisions.
- `core/interop_gateway.py` queues signed, minimized OCSF/STIX/OTLP envelopes.
  External egress is denied by default. Preserve idempotency, backoff, and
  dead-letter bounds; connectors must verify before delivery.
- `docs/enterprise/` is authoritative for supported-edition claims,
  compatibility, architecture decisions, detection-content governance, and
  support/security operations. Code and marketing must stay within those gates.
- `core/fleet_hunts.py` permits only registered artifact types and exact targets.
  It forbids command/shell/script/path input, enforces host/byte/time/expiry
  budgets, independent approvals, authenticated durable state, and receipts.
- `core/hunt_workspace.py` is the non-executable hunt notebook and result layer.
  It accepts typed `HuntQuery` objects, bounded notes/findings/decisions, and
  immutable digest references; optimistic revisions prevent lost updates.
  HMAC-authenticated atomic state fails closed on tampering. Sanitized export
  redacts identities/paths, omits device tokens and raw artifacts, and excludes
  restricted results. Never add code cells, arbitrary paths, or a shell.
- `core/hunt_operations.py` persists HMAC-authenticated per-host progress and
  coded failures, enforces non-regressing timestamps/bytes plus hunt host/byte
  budgets, and produces authenticated bounded summaries. Promotion uses a
  deterministic case identity, immutable result references, idempotency, and
  CaseStore custody verification; it never copies raw artifacts.
- `core/safe_response_session.py` creates maximum-30-minute sessions bound to
  one target, requester, registered query set, and registered Response Broker
  operation set. Read-only sessions require one independent approval; sessions
  with host changes require two, and every operation still requires its separate
  risk-based approval. Executable fields and capability escape fail closed.
  Transcript events store action identity/outcome and request/result digests,
  form an HMAC-authenticated chain, persist atomically, and replay idempotently.
  Query handlers run outside the session lock; close/expiry stays responsive and
  a late result is transcripted as discarded rather than returned.
- `core/atomic_io.py:replace_with_retry()` handles only short antivirus/sharing
  locks with a bounded exponential retry. It must not suppress persistent or
  unrelated filesystem errors.
- `core/reliability_lab.py` runs only registered, deterministic recovery drills
  with explicit retryable exception classes, bounded attempts/delay/timeout,
  and content-addressed evidence. Current tests cover transient database lock,
  permanent collector outage, unknown failure surfacing, supervised fleet
  service restart, and interoperability dead-letter exhaustion. This is not
  8-hour/24-hour/7-day physical-host soak proof.
- `core/release_evidence.py` and `tools/run_release_gate.py` define the fixed
  local release gate: serial pytest, bytecode, Ruff, pip-audit, and documentation
  drift. The pack binds the full commit, source epoch, redacted summaries,
  command/output digests, limitations, and manifest digest. It is
  content-addressed local evidence; publisher signature remains externally gated.
- `resilience/recovery_state.py`, `resilience/supervisor.py`, and
  `resilience/diagnostics.py` implement stateful recovery. Core Manager and peer
  Watchdog use separate HMAC-authenticated atomic ledgers. A dead/suspended
  component receives a bounded authenticated health snapshot before exponential
  backoff; rolling failure budgets, restart deadlines, diagnostic digests, and
  safe mode survive a supervisor restart. Tampered state fails closed until an
  authenticated manual restart resets it. Stopped heartbeats and signed
  stand-down do not respawn.
- `core/backup_restore.py` is the streaming encrypted backup and approval-gated
  restore boundary. It snapshots regular files and SQLite databases under the
  canonical data root, rejects path traversal/symlink/reparse input and an
  in-root archive destination, encrypts the complete tar stream with AES-GCM,
  and signs receipts separately. Restore re-verifies the archive, requires the
  suite offline and two distinct non-requester approvers, stages every item,
  retains previous files under `.restore-rollback/<plan>`, and rolls back an
  interrupted replacement. Never embed the encryption key in the archive.
- `core/recovery_policy.py` is side-effect-free policy and evidence. It computes
  disabled-by-default cadence status, exact selection/destination coverage,
  verified-copy floors, count/age retention, and HMAC-authenticated deletion
  proposals but never schedules work or deletes an archive. Named site-loss,
  database-corruption, control-plane-compromise, bad-policy/update, and
  lost-signing-key objectives define Recovery Point Objective (RPO), Recovery
  Time Objective (RTO), copy count, owner, and review. Drill evidence measures
  RPO/RTO and requires archive, manifest, service-health, and rollback proof.
- `core/audit_export.py` creates exact tenant/scope/time-bounded audit exchanges.
  Restricted fields are removed; sensitive fields and actors are tokenized;
  free text is redacted; truncation is explicit. Every record binds its
  predecessor and the manifest HMAC binds the chain head and records digest.
- Normal launch never rewrites the elevated autostart task. Only an explicit
  Settings state change may mutate startup registration.
- Development gates are pinned in `pyproject.toml`: Hypothesis 6.163.0,
  Ruff 0.16.0, pytest-xdist 3.8.0, and pip-audit 2.10.1. Hypothesis properties
  are deterministic, database-free, synthetic, and offline; they are a
  development extra, never a product runtime dependency. Ruff uses
  correctness-critical rules first. Keep the complete suite serial because
  Windows ACL tests are not process-parallel-safe; xdist is for isolated groups.
- `tools/github_toolkit.lock.json` pins development-only GitHub assets and
  SHA-256 digests: uv 0.12.0, py-spy 0.4.2, hyperfine 1.20.0, and official
  GitHub CLI 2.96.0. The bootstrap keeps them in ignored `.dev-tools` and
  creates a separate Bandit 1.9.4, Vulture 2.16, and pytest-timeout 2.4.0
  environment. None are product runtime dependencies. The first Bandit pass
  found and closed the high-confidence SHA-1 identifier and shell-clearing
  findings; the high-severity re-scan is clean.
- `core/drill_resolution.py`, `modules/purple_guard.py`,
  `modules/posture_hardening.py`, and `shark/aar_report.py` implement
  proof-driven benign-drill closure. Each unique actionable technique receives
  a typed HMAC-authenticated action contract with exact scope, preconditions,
  operator-reviewed authorization, safety checks, idempotency, verification
  expiry, exact rollback, and individually authenticated apply/verify/rollback
  receipts. Contracts contain no command, shell, script, code, or arbitrary
  executable fields.
- Detector policy installation and inert-marker cleanup are APPLIED state only.
  Only an exact Purple Remediation Guard echo from a different signed run,
  technique-bound to the active contract and observed after application, can
  produce VERIFIED_CLOSED. Wrong run, detector, technique, contract ID/digest,
  pre-apply evidence, and tampered lifecycle state fail closed. A future miss or
  expired verification reopens the issue; repeated occurrences are idempotent.
- AAR scoring separates detection coverage, correlated same-run SOAR response,
  deterministic action application, and verified closure. Closure uses unique
  actionable technique classes, so repeated campaign steps do not inflate the
  numerator or denominator; unmonitored/no-detector-by-design and resilience
  stages remain outside it. Do not collapse these four metrics.
- Purple Guard rollback removes only the exact technique policy and preserves
  unrelated detector candidates. Short antivirus sharing locks use the existing
  bounded atomic-replacement retry; persistent filesystem failures remain visible.
- `start-angerona.bat` validates the elevated source volume with
  `System.IO.DriveInfo` and `System.IO.DriveType.Fixed`. Do not use
  `FileSystemInfo.PSDrive.DriveType`: that property is blank for normal path
  items and caused valid D: source checkouts to fail closed before launch.
  Reparse-point and required-file checks remain, followed by the independent
  Python source/interpreter trust preflight.
- `tests/test_property_fuzz_boundaries.py` is the deterministic trust-boundary
  property suite. Every parser must normalize completely or raise its documented
  validation error. It covers sensor envelopes, signed capability manifests,
  detection packages, fleet authentication, authenticated IPC frames,
  encrypted-backup metadata, portable restore paths, signed release envelopes,
  portable ZIP metadata, and bounded Sigma YAML documents. Keep `database=None`,
  `derandomize=True`, bounded examples, no network, and no real endpoint data.
  The first passes closed
  malformed platform/header exception leaks, schema smuggling, silent list
  truncation, non-finite values, and Windows alternate-data-stream/device-alias
  paths. `core/archive_safety.py` now gives update packages, verified offline
  speech models, and inert drill-marker readers one canonical pre-read contract:
  bounded entry/member/expanded sizes and ratios, canonical portable paths,
  Unicode normalization, duplicate/case-collision rejection, and no encryption,
  unsupported compression, symlinks, or special files. Update envelopes use
  exact schemas and strict Ed25519 signature encoding; speech redirects remain
  on the approved HTTPS origin. Sigma imports reject aliases, non-plain/nonfinite
  types, and excessive bytes/documents/nodes/depth. Current local user-mode
  document/archive fuzz coverage is complete; any future native driver IOCTL
  remains a separate conditional gate.
- `resilience/ipc_ring.py` v2 is the scanner-to-core trust boundary. Every fixed
  slot carries a full-sequence HMAC-SHA-256 tag under a dedicated protected
  per-install key. Decode must verify exact schema, sensor, 64-bit ring position,
  payload, and tag before returning bytes. Wrong-key, tampered, replayed,
  out-of-position, unknown-schema, oversized, symlink-backed, or malformed
  input fails closed. The process-creation payload parser accepts only strict
  UTF-8 JSON with exact fields and finite bounded types. Manager rejection
  metrics and rate-limited alerts never retain the rejected raw payload.
  Do not claim process isolation: a fully compromised scanner that can read the
  ring key can forge a valid record. Code integrity, process supervision, and
  future native isolation remain separate controls.
- `gui/telemetry_worker.py` enforces long-runtime backpressure at both sides of
  its queued signal. Pending and UI queues retain the newest 2,000 events,
  signal/render batches are capped at 250, EventBus identity history retains
  4,096 `(object identity, timestamp)` pairs, and snapshots expose drops. Stop
  clears the UI queue and rejects late results. Do not replace these with
  unbounded lists/sets. A 100,000-event synthetic burst retained 2,000 and
  accounted for 98,000 drops in 216.46 ms.
- `gui/system_pulse.py` ignores late samples after shutdown.
  ARIA voice resolver/listener startup and the complete self-test are
  single-flight. Canary echo ingestion is non-blocking and retains the newest
  64 records. Existing generation, shutdown-drain, sleep/resume, and closed
  dialog tests complete the concurrency/lifecycle contract.
- Windows source startup runs `tools/protect-key-custody.ps1` before any
  runtime key access. Keep `icacls /setowner` and DACL `/reset` as separate
  native command forms; Windows rejects a combined ownership/DACL invocation.
  The migration closes the root first, rejects reparse points, resets
  descendants, quarantines pre-existing bus/shutdown keys, and writes
  `.custody-v1` only after success. Visible phase messages are intentional
  because a first migration of a large report/model tree can take time.
- `core/endpoint_identity.py` binds initial enrollment IDs to their Ed25519
  public key, signs identity/access state v2, and verifies rotation only against
  the caller's already-trusted old ID/key. Never restore self-signed arbitrary
  device IDs or unsigned/downgraded state.
- `core/plugin_lifecycle.py` treats its catalog as untrusted input: exact schema,
  duplicate rejection, portable one-file entrypoints, size/type/time/digest
  bounds, root confinement, reparse rejection, and activation-time capability,
  entrypoint, and source-digest rebinding. `ModuleManager` permits unsigned
  hash-pinned development modules only when both development flags are explicit
  and protected key-custody mode is off. Canonical launchers force that override
  off.
- `core/ai_security_broker.py` treats every model response as untrusted JSON.
  It requires exact fields, cited known evidence, finite bounded values, and a
  registered typed tool schema. Every validated response receives a private
  broker HMAC; execution authorizations expire in 1-300 seconds, are consumed
  before handler entry, cannot cross brokers or be replayed, and retain at most
  4,096 live replay entries. Handler results are bounded finite JSON. Audit
  receipts require a response authenticated by that broker and are HMAC
  verified. AI mutation still belongs behind the separate Response Broker,
  never a raw shell/code tool.
- ENT-QA-005 is complete for current local user-mode surfaces: a 74-test
  selection covers forged identity/policy/update/receipt/AAR, tenant isolation,
  replay/expiry, path traversal/symlink/reparse, untrusted plugins, and prompt
  injection/tool abuse.
- Current Cycle 8 evidence: 522 passed / 2 intentional platform skips; compile
  and Ruff clean; no known installed-package vulnerability reported.

## CYCLE 9 - FIVE-LOOP SECURITY, PERFORMANCE, AND ENTERPRISE EVIDENCE

- `core/url_policy.py` is the single outbound transport boundary. Public HTTPS
  retrieval rejects credentials, private/loopback/link-local/metadata targets,
  unsafe redirects, oversize requests/responses, and unapproved hosts. Local
  service JSON is loopback-only and bounded. Do not restore direct product
  `requests.get/post` or `urllib.request.urlopen` callers.
- XML consumers use `defusedxml` plus explicit byte limits. Archive, JSON, YAML,
  process-baseline, and fleet inputs remain exact-schema, bounded, and
  reparse-aware. Malformed external input must fail closed without leaking a
  local path or raw payload into diagnostics.
- `engines/ollama_client.py` is the guarded local model choke point. All
  generation callers use it. It enforces loopback, endpoint allowlisting,
  bounded request/NDJSON response, safe errors, and full-output redaction before
  emitting stream chunks. Diagnostics expose only aggregate timing; never cache
  prompts or model responses for World View.
- World View must not create synthetic generations to measure Ollama. It reads
  `diagnostics_snapshot()` from the latest real inference. The AI proxy keeps
  upstream work off its event loop, and cloud code synthesis stays disabled
  unless `ANGERONA_CLOUD_CODE_SYNTHESIS=1` is explicitly set.
- Long-runtime queues and text histories are fixed-size newest-retained buffers.
  Voice and legacy publishers use non-blocking drop-oldest behavior. Hidden
  Threat Intel polling stops until show. Do not add unbounded histories or
  blocking persistence/model/network work to the Qt thread or EventBus path.
- Startup optional-service failures publish signed, privacy-minimized Startup
  Health events. Protection module loader failure is Critical. Store impact and
  exception type, not raw exceptions, paths, credentials, or source content.
- Fleet Preview now initializes `EndpointIdentity` under the configured data
  root, registers its Ed25519 public identity with the tenant-scoped local plane,
  and stores only an HMAC-derived hostname token. The service remains disabled
  by default and loopback-only; no public/LAN listener or generic remote shell.
- Enterprise Readiness assessment v2 separates local engineering maturity from
  production deployment gates. It credits shipped and tested identity, scoped
  Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), signed policy/canary, backup/restore, release,
  audit, privacy, integrity, and storage controls. It must continue to list
  mutual Transport Layer Security (mTLS), Single Sign-On (SSO) / OpenID Connect
  (OIDC), high availability/disaster-recovery proof, and publisher signing as
  external requirements.
- `evidence_pack()` is deterministic, content-addressed, bounded to 128 KiB, and
  public-safe. It contains low-cardinality runtime state only: never add
  hostnames, usernames, paths, credentials, event payloads, private/public keys,
  endpoint identifiers, prompts, or model responses.
- Final Cycle 9 evidence: 556 passed / 2 intentional platform skips / 0 failed;
  Python compilation and Ruff clean. The release evidence pack records the
  fixed bytecode, dependency-audit, documentation-drift, lint, and serial-test
  gates. Publisher signing, repository rulesets, external penetration testing,
  long physical-host soaks, independent disaster-recovery exercises, and
  production mTLS/OIDC/HA remain external gates.

## CYCLE 10 - FLEET INTEGRITY AND ACCESS GOVERNANCE

- `core/fleet_control_plane.py` treats endpoint time and content as untrusted.
  Event bodies are copied into bounded plain JSON and reject non-string/empty/
  oversized keys, non-finite numbers, integers outside signed 64-bit range,
  invalid UTF-8, custom objects, cycles, and depth/node/container/byte overflow.
  Keep these checks before hashing or SQLite insertion.
- Fleet event identity is `(tenant_id, event_id)` plus a permanent device and
  body binding. An exact retry may return `duplicate=True`, but it must retain
  the original observed time, server receipt time, clock classification, skew,
  device identity, and event hash. Never accept the same ID from a different
  device even when the body hash matches.
- Endpoint `observed_at` is never inventory liveness. `received_at` comes from
  the control-plane clock and updates device `last_seen`. Clock quality is one
  of `synchronized`, `skewed`, `untrusted`, `server-assigned`, or `legacy`;
  non-finite/non-positive timestamps fail. Legacy databases add the new columns
  in place and backfill explicit legacy uncertainty without deleting events.
- `ingestion_health()` is tenant-authorized and low-cardinality. It exposes
  stored events, duplicate retries, clock-quality counts, last receipt time, and
  device-state counts; it never returns event payloads. The public readiness
  snapshot further removes tenant and device identity and keeps only bounded
  counts/state plus the public API-contract digest.
- `core/fleet_service.py::openapi_contract()` is the deterministic OpenAPI 3.1
  source for routes actually implemented. Canonical device, event, ingestion-
  health, and `/v1/openapi` routes use the same complete-path/query/body HMAC,
  freshness, and durable nonce replay boundary. `/health` is the only unsigned
  route and discloses only service/loopback/version/contract-digest state. Do not
  advertise production mTLS, remote exposure, case/search APIs, or high
  availability through this local contract.
- The fleet HTTP boundary accepts POST bodies only as `application/json`, caps
  content length, returns no-store/nosniff headers, and suppresses the Python
  runtime version from the Server header. Do not add a generic command route.
- `core/authorization.py::STANDARD_ROLES` is the canonical nine-role catalog:
  Viewer, Analyst, Hunter, Responder, Detection Engineer, Fleet Operator,
  Tenant Administrator, Platform Administrator, and Auditor. Permissions remain
  default-deny and scoped. `DEFAULT_DUTY_CONSTRAINTS` rejects overlapping
  auditor/operational and detection-author/policy-approver bindings before the
  policy hash is created. Response Broker still enforces distinct requesters and
  approvers at action time; external identity and release-key ceremony remain
  separate gates.
- Enterprise Readiness assessment v3 includes bounded fleet-ingestion state,
  event/uncertain-clock counts, and the public OpenAPI digest. The copy actions
  in Enterprise Settings must never include a tenant ID, endpoint ID, hostname,
  username, local path, payload, service key, or identity key.
- Final Cycle 10 evidence: 576 passed / 2 intentional platform skips / 0 failed;
  full Ruff and Python compilation clean; focused Bandit medium/high clean.
  Production mTLS, SSO/OIDC, protected publisher signing, repository rulesets,
  HA/DR infrastructure, external penetration review, and physical-host soaks
  remain external gates.

## CYCLE 11 - ATOMIC FLEET DELIVERY

- `core/fleet_control_plane.py::ingest_batch()` is the single event write path.
  It accepts 1-256 mapping envelopes, normalizes every event before acquiring
  the database write lock, caps each event at 256 KiB and the aggregate normalized
  payload at 4 MiB, and commits or rolls back the complete batch. Keep single-
  event `ingest()` as a one-item wrapper so validation and idempotency cannot
  drift between APIs.
- Batch envelope fields are exactly `device_id`, `event_id`, `body`, and optional
  `observed_at`. Unknown fields, missing required fields, non-mapping events,
  invalid device/event identifiers, non-plain JSON, and invalid timestamps fail
  before persistence. Never silently truncate an oversized batch.
- Device state is read only for the distinct endpoint identifiers named by the
  batch. Every named device must be enrolled and active. Revoked, quarantined,
  retired, or absent devices fail the transaction before any event, last-seen,
  or health-counter change survives.
- At-least-once semantics remain device-bound. An exact retry returns a signed
  duplicate receipt with the original chronology; changed evidence or reuse by
  another endpoint rolls the entire batch back. Multiple events in a batch do
  not imply total ordering across endpoints or sensors.
- Batch health updates are aggregate and low-cardinality: accepted batches,
  attempted event count, largest batch, stored events, duplicates, and clock
  classifications. Do not add payloads, hostnames, user names, local paths,
  endpoint identifiers, or keys to this health view.
- `core/fleet_service.py` OpenAPI contract version 1.1.0 publishes the
  authenticated `/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/event-batches` route and 256-event
  limit. Request freshness, full path/query/body HMAC, durable nonce replay
  defense, loopback binding, JSON media type, and request byte cap remain
  unchanged. Compression and adaptive flow control are not yet advertised.
- Final Cycle 11 evidence: 580 passed / 2 intentional platform skips / 0 failed;
  full Ruff and Python compilation clean; focused Bandit medium/high clean.
  Production mTLS, remote quotas/rate limits, compression negotiation, high
  availability, and physical-host fault/soak evidence remain separate gates.

## CYCLES 12-13 - COMPRESSED DELIVERY AND ADMISSION CONTROL

- Fleet request authentication always covers the exact wire body. Only after a
  fresh complete-target HMAC and one-time nonce pass may `fleet_service.py`
  decode the body. Identity and gzip are the only supported encodings.
- Gzip decoding uses a bounded single-member stream. Reject malformed streams,
  incomplete streams, concatenated members, trailing bytes, and output beyond
  5 MiB before JSON parsing. The 256 KiB per-event and 4 MiB aggregate normalized
  batch limits remain independent checks after decoding. Never replace this with
  an unbounded `gzip.decompress()` call on request data.
- OpenAPI contract version 1.2.0 and authenticated
  `/v1/ingestion-capabilities` are the deterministic transport-negotiation
  sources. They publish supported encodings, fixed wire/decoded/normalized/item
  budgets, compression threshold, and default admission budgets without tenant,
  endpoint, payload, path, user, host, or key identity.
- `FleetIngestionRateLimiter` enforces bounded token buckets per authorized
  tenant and active endpoint. It runs inside the fleet transaction after all
  named devices are proven active and before event lookup/insertion. A denied
  batch rolls the transaction back and raises `FleetRateLimitError` with a
  bounded retry delay; the HTTP service maps that to 429 and Retry-After.
- Admission attempts count even if later evidence conflict checks fail. This is
  intentional abuse resistance. Durable stored/duplicate/clock/batch counters
  and device liveness still remain unchanged on rollback. Admission health is
  explicitly process-local and resets at restart.
- Rate state has a hard bucket bound and never creates identities for missing or
  inactive devices. Do not move admission after persistence or silently evict
  an active bucket to admit attacker-controlled identities.
- Final Cycle 13 evidence: 586 passed / 2 intentional platform skips / 0 failed;
  full Ruff and Python compilation clean; focused Bandit medium/high clean.
  Production distributed quotas, adaptive endpoint backpressure, mTLS, high
  availability, and physical-host storm/full-disk drills remain separate gates.

## NEVER DO
- **Cycle 7 enterprise foundations (newest, 2026-07-29)** — The authoritative
  flight recorder and normalized evidence path use bounded asynchronous workers,
  batching, observable overflow/dead-letter state, and shutdown draining.
  Signed detection content revalidates content, signature, current key trust,
  and expiry. Endpoint enrollment/replay controls, signed policy rollout,
  scoped fleet jobs, asset inventory, operational objectives, case custody,
  privacy governance, AI brokering, release assurance, and scoped RBAC have
  deterministic local contracts and tests.
- **Cycle 7 security closure** — Case exports redact credentials, identities,
  and user paths and omit restricted references/comment bodies. Custody chains
  use authenticated heads and signed retention receipts. Authorization receipts
  bind principal, permission, canonical scope, resource, policy, and request
  digest; conflicting request IDs fail within a bounded 10,000-entry local
  window. A future cross-process broker requires durable replay storage.
- **AI/remediation boundary** — Model-generated PowerShell is staged only as
  `.ps1.txt`; generated Python is staged only as `.py.review`. Never execute,
  hot-load, or append generated code to live source. Reviewed extensions must
  use the signed Capability Manifest path on restart.
- **Newest verification** — full pytest 334 passed / 2 intentional platform
  skips / 0 failed; headless self-check 26/26; compile, workflow-policy, and
  dependency checks clean. Authenticode, branch rules, external labs, production
  driver qualification, and Apple notarization remain external gates.
- **Enterprise foundations (newest)** — `core/evidence_store.py` adds versioned local evidence plus typed bounded hunting; `core/detection_packages.py` adds digest-verified, non-executable detection packages; `core/exposure_recovery.py` adds explainable exposure scoring and planning-only recovery contracts with prerequisites, verification, rollback, and human review.
- **Integration boundary** — do not synchronously attach SQLite evidence writes to EventBus producer threads. Live wiring requires a bounded asynchronous ingest queue with backpressure, batching, metrics, and shutdown draining.
- **Newest verification** — focused foundation tests 14/14; full pytest 237 passed / 2 intentional platform skips / 0 failed; compile 236/236. This does not claim completed enterprise parity: fleet RBAC, signed content distribution, privileged containment, collectors, recovery execution, and signed supply-chain delivery remain gated.
- Never edit an unrelated terminal prototype outside this repository for GUI changes.
- NEVER block the Qt main thread; module work runs in BaseModule daemon threads; GUI updates via signals/QTimer.
- NEVER auto-execute a remediation or custom patch — always review-gated; loopback (Ollama :11434, IPC) stays reachable.
- NEVER add a second app instance (singleton :47921) or bypass the STOP/kill-all hard shutdown.
- NEVER send host data off-machine without consent; Ollama local-first, cloud only on threshold via `cloud_fallback`.
- NEVER enable Remote Bridge (RBRG) implicitly — it is the ONLY off-box egress path. It stays `enabled_by_default=False` and must not open a socket without an explicit shared key + peer. HWID DPAPI-wraps the IPC key but must NEVER mutate the live `ipc_auth.key` AUTH reads (protected sidecar only).
